prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (max 500 words)

- Constitutional and governance
  - Seek a referendum on independence and expanded powers for the Scottish Parliament.
  - Introduce a written constitution with inclusive citizenship criteria; retain the monarch as head of state subject to referendum.
  - Use proportional representation for all elections.
  - Reduce and reform quangos; increase parliamentary oversight.
  - Support civil service career development within Scotland.

- Public finance and investment
  - Establish a sovereign wealth fund from oil revenues to finance services sustainably.
  - Create a not‑for‑profit public investment vehicle to replace costly PFI/PPP and accelerate infrastructure delivery.
  - Conduct a comprehensive tax review to simplify, increase transparency, and avoid raising the overall burden; consider a local income tax.
  - Immediately cut fuel duty by 10p per gallon, funded by a new top income tax supplement on very high earners.

- Economy, jobs and wages
  - Major infrastructure and broadband rollout; streamline enterprise agencies; stronger international marketing for trade and tourism.
  - Devolve and refocus employment programmes on skills and long‑term unemployment.
  - Raise the minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages and pursue further increases; end age differentials.
  - Enact a statutory charter of trade union rights.

- Education, children and students
  - Abolish tuition fees; rebuild maintenance grants; support further student support reforms.
  - Lower the voting age to 16; fully implement UN children’s rights and create a Children’s Commissioner.
  - Establish an Education Convention and pause further system changes; reduce P1–P3 class sizes to 18.
  - End school league tables, reduce testing burden, and refurbish schools via public investment.
  - Expand Gaelic‑medium education; protect rural schools; strengthen inclusion, ICT training, and Scottish studies.

- Health and care
  - Create a National Health Care Commission to set strategy and end postcode treatment; make technology assessment decisions binding and expand capacity.
  - Provide free fruit in primary schools and set nutritional standards for school meals.
  - Reintroduce free dental check‑ups; freeze and review prescription charges.
  - Invest in equipment and cleanliness; recruit at least 1,500 nurses; halve maximum inpatient waiting times.
  - Provide free personal care for older people.

- Environment, energy and water
  - Develop a national climate strategy; expand renewables; no new nuclear stations and planned decommissioning.
  - Promote resource efficiency and empower the environmental regulator over defence sites.
  - Review water industry finances, protect low‑income users, democratise governance, and prevent privatisation by stealth.

- Transport
  - Secure a fair share of UK investment; establish regional transport authorities and a single safety regulator; keep air traffic control public.
  - Take a public stake in rail infrastructure; reopen lines and electrify key routes; add airport rail links.
  - Create a national concessionary travel scheme; maintain roads and target bottlenecks.
  - Reduce ferry fares (including RET pilots) and abolish Skye Bridge tolls; increase direct international flights.

- Rural, agriculture and fisheries
  - Support rural small businesses, digital adoption, fuel duty cuts, transport, and key local services.
  - Post‑outbreak agricultural review; align EU rule timing to preserve competitiveness; promote diversification and quality produce; mitigate Less Favoured Areas impacts.
  - Use compensated tie‑ups and technical conservation; decentralise fisheries management; back processing and aquaculture; commission a salmon‑farming inquiry and long‑term strategy.

- Housing, communities and social policy
  - Seek UK assumption of historic council housing debt; devolve housing benefit; invest via public investment vehicle.
  - Oppose wholesale stock transfer; strengthen tenant rights.
  - Provide three‑year core funding and water‑charge relief for voluntary groups; tackle rough sleeping and hidden homelessness.
  - Restore the earnings link for the basic pension using National Insurance surplus; aim to align the basic pension with the minimum income guarantee over time.
  - Streamline benefits delivery into a single agency; simplify housing benefit; improve disability and carers’ support; extend winter fuel help to severely disabled people; review support for 16–17‑year‑olds; reduce high marginal tax rates in in‑work benefits; boost benefit take‑up.

- Justice and policing
  - Fund 1,000 additional police officers; expand drug courts and rehabilitation.
  - Allow parental compensation orders for youth damage.
  - Introduce lifetime supervision for high‑risk offenders; extend supervised release; create a sentencing advisory panel; speed up lower courts.

- Europe, defence and international
  - Support EU membership with stronger subsidiarity and fisheries reform; adopt the euro only with economic conditions and referendum.
  - Remove nuclear weapons; oppose missile defence; phase out participation in nuclear alliances while maintaining defence cooperation; form a professional defence force.
  - Consolidate overseas promotion of trade, investment and tourism within the existing budget.
  - Increase development aid, untie assistance, and support debt relief.
</text>
